top_signal.title: Started a hospitality recruitment business in the Netherlands — 25 cold calls in, zero clients. Is the market too small or is my positioning off?
top_signal.summary: Not sure if there are any Dutch people here, but any input is welcome.   I recently started my own recruitment and selection company. The model is simple: I recruit part-time staff for hospitality businesses — servers, bar, kitchen help, dishwashers. I find the candidates through social media and through a youth employment organisation I work with, screen them myself, and only pass on the ones I think fit. The restaurant does the actual interview and hires the person directly. No cure, no pay — they only pay if they hire someone. Flat fee of €750, no percentage, plus a one-month replacement guarantee.   I've called about 25 places so far. A few showed real interest — one confirmed they needed kitchen and dishwashing staff, a couple asked me to send information — but nothing has converted yet. The most common answer is that they don't have a shortage, or that recruiting doesn't cost them much effort because they just post on Instagram or hire through their own staff.   That last part is what worries me. If finding part-time people genuinely isn't a problem for them, my whole service doesn't have a reason to exist.   So my question: is there a better way to position this so it actually lands with owners? Or is part-time hospitality recruitment just a market too small to be worth the time?
